scams.name: Fake Terracotta Army Site & 'Shortcut' Tour
scams.description: One of China's most documented tourist scams: a taxi or 'cheap tour' from Xi'an city centre pulls up to a venue marked 'Terracotta Warriors' or 'Qin Museum' that is NOT the real Emperor Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum. The real Terracotta Army site is at Lintong, 35 km east of Xi'an, operated by Shaanxi Provincial Bureau of Cultural Heritage. Fake venues on the route show mass-produced warrior replicas, charge ¥100–¥200 entry, and are a complete fraud. The canonical community warning — titled 'Don't be scammed in Xi'an in visiting the fake terracotta army' — remains referenced through 2025. Another traveler confirmed: 'there are fake terracotta attractions in xi'an that would scam tourists with the entire thing' — entire faux-archaeological sites built to deceive. The related scam is the 'all-inclusive' tour: community reports document the bait-and-switch pattern where tourists book a ¥150 'Terracotta tour' that turns out to be 80% shopping stops at jade factories, tea 'museums,' and silk 'factories' — each paying commission to the guide. The real Terracotta Army visit gets 60–90 minutes before the bus moves to the next shopping stop. 2025 community reports confirm the current method: book direct via the official Bingmayong WeChat mini-program or the Ctrip/Trip.com app at ¥120 adult (¥100 low season). For older travelers, the clean route: (1) take the official Tourist Bus Line 5 (游5) from Xi'an Railway Station East Plaza to Lintong — ¥8 one-way, 1 hour, departures every 20 minutes; (2) book the Terracotta Warriors entry ticket (¥120 adult) via the official WeChat mini-program 'Qin Shi Huang Di Ling Bowu Yuan' (秦始皇帝陵博物院) or on Trip.com; (3) for a guided experience, book a licensed small-group tour via Viator, GetYourGuide, or your hotel's Ctrip partnership — verify ZERO shopping stops in writing before paying; (4) NEVER accept 'discount Terracotta tour' offers from taxi drivers, hotel-lobby booths under ¥200, or touts at Xi'an Railway Station.
scams.avoidance: Take Tourist Bus Line 5 (游5) from Xi'an Railway Station East Plaza — ¥8, 1 hour, every 20 min Book entry ticket (¥120 adult) at the official WeChat mini-program 'Qin Shi Huang Di Ling Bowu Yuan' or Trip.com For guided tours, use Viator, GetYourGuide, or hotel Ctrip partnership; verify ZERO shopping stops in writing Reject any tour booth at Xi'an Railway Station or hotel lobby offering 'discount Terracotta tour' under ¥200 Confirm the destination as 'Emperor Qin Shi Huang's Mausoleum Site Museum' — nothing else
scams.location: Outside Xi'an city centre on the road to Lintong; fake 'Terracotta Museum' venues along the route, hotel lobby tour-booth referrals

scams.name: Muslim Quarter Tourist-Menu & 'Famous' Food Stall Overcharge
scams.description: The Muslim Quarter's main street (Beiyuanmen, just north of the Drum Tower) is Xi'an's most-photographed food-tourism street. It is also, per 2025 community reports: 'The famous Muslim Quarter Main Street is crowded and expensive. Eat here instead' — meaning locals avoid it. One 2025 insider guide tells foreign visitors to eat ONE street off the main strip for 1/3 the price and better quality. Common overcharges: ¥30–¥50 for a single yangrou paomo (lamb bread soup) that costs ¥15–¥20 one street over; ¥40–¥60 for 'famous' biangbiang noodles that cost ¥15–¥25; ¥35 per skewer of lamb that should be ¥5–¥10. The Muslim Quarter also hosts a documented 'Xinjiang cake' scam — a dried-fruit-and-nut bar cut from a wheel displayed on a cart. Vendors cut a small-looking piece and weigh it in grams; the 'small piece' turns out to be 200+ grams at ¥12/gram, producing a ¥2,000+ bill for what looked like a snack. 2025 community reports document the ongoing concern: 'They were sometimes involved in scam fruitcake sales (you'd know if you saw it)' — the scam is so widely documented it has a Wikipedia-level reputation. Other travelers place the Xinjiang cake scam in the short list of 'first-time China trip' experiences to avoid. For older travelers, the defence: (1) walk one street off Beiyuanmen to Huajue Xiang or Xiyangshi Street where locals eat at posted-price stalls; (2) for specific honest venues, Yongxing Fang (a 2018-opened food court showcasing Shaanxi cuisine with posted prices), Lao Sun Jia (established 1898, yangrou paomo ¥45 per bowl), Jia San Guantang Baozi (¥30 per basket of soup dumplings) are all community-verified; (3) NEVER buy 'Xinjiang cake' from a pushcart vendor — even if you want to try it, buy a pre-packaged version at a supermarket for ¥5–¥15; (4) for all food stalls, ask 'duo shao qian' (how much) and confirm the price before the vendor starts cutting or serving.
scams.avoidance: Eat one street off Beiyuanmen: Huajue Xiang, Xiyangshi Street, or Yongxing Fang food court Community-verified venues: Lao Sun Jia (yangrou paomo ¥45), Jia San (soup dumplings ¥30), Yongxing Fang (posted prices) NEVER buy 'Xinjiang cake' from a pushcart — supermarket pre-packaged versions are ¥5–¥15 Confirm 'duo shao qian' (how much) BEFORE the vendor starts cutting or serving Reject any tout pulling you toward a restaurant with English-photo menus
scams.location: Muslim Quarter (Beiyuanmen / North Gate Market) main street, around Drum Tower south entrance, Huimin Street

scams.name: Xi'an Airport (XIY) Taxi Overcharge & Station Touts
scams.description: Xi'an Xianyang International Airport (XIY) is 40 km north-west of the city centre. The legitimate metered taxi fare is ¥120–¥160 (about 45 min). Unofficial drivers inside the terminal approach with 'fixed price 300! 400!' and refuse the meter. One 2025 traveler summed it up: 'They are scams and trying to overcharge you. It's unbearable. Go straight to the real taxi stand' — the rule is universal across Chinese airports and applies at XIY. Another 2025 report documents the subtler variant: 'If the driver wanted to scam you, they could have just taken a slightly longer detour. The Didi platform has safety controls that actually detect this' — meaning DiDi's GPS-verified routing catches route-padding that licensed street taxis can still get away with. The alternative transport options at XIY: (1) the airport Metro Line 14 runs to Xi'an Railway Station (¥17, 70 min) — slower but scam-proof; (2) the airport shuttle bus to Xi'an Railway Station (¥25, 60 min) and Longhai Hotel (¥30); (3) DiDi at the official rideshare pickup zone with app-regulated fares (¥120–¥150 estimate). Community reports flag a related airport scam: 'One scam thieves do is trick you into using your phone, such as I lost my phone in a taxi, and I need to call' — a stranger at arrivals asks to borrow your phone and either walks off with it or uses it to log into your mobile-banking or WeChat. For older travelers arriving at XIY after an international flight, the protective playbook: (1) pre-install DiDi with international number before flying; (2) walk past anyone soliciting taxi rides inside the terminal; (3) use the airport Metro Line 14 or shuttle bus if you have time-flexibility; (4) if taking a licensed taxi, insist on 'da biao' (打表) and screenshot a DiDi fare estimate as reference; (5) NEVER hand your unlocked phone to a stranger for any reason — if anyone at the airport asks to 'borrow' your phone, it is a scam.
scams.avoidance: Install DiDi before flying with international number; use at official rideshare pickup zone Take airport Metro Line 14 (¥17, 70 min) or shuttle bus (¥25, 60 min) for scam-proof option If licensed taxi, say 'da biao' (打表) before boarding; confirm ¥120–¥160 range NEVER hand your unlocked phone to any stranger at the airport Photograph taxi plate number from rear windscreen on entering
scams.location: Xi'an Xianyang International Airport (XIY) arrivals, Xi'an Railway Station East Plaza, Xi'an North High-Speed Rail Station

scams.name: Bell Tower & Drum Tower Area Pickpockets
scams.description: Xi'an's pedestrian core — Bell Tower, Drum Tower, and the Ancient City Wall — draws massive tour-group traffic, particularly in summer peak and during Spring Festival. 2025 community guides capture the picture: moderate opportunistic pickpocketing at the tourist choke points, much less than Barcelona-level but present during peak crowds. Community reports show the typical first-time-visitor itinerary and concentration of tour buses at these sites. The risk zones: (1) Bell Tower underground passage (the pedestrian tunnel connecting all four sides) during 10 AM and 2 PM tour-bus arrivals; (2) Drum Tower's Muslim Quarter south entrance where food crowds and tour groups mix; (3) City Wall South Gate (Yongningmen) ticket office queue and bike-rental station; (4) Big Wild Goose Pagoda square during evening fountain show. Other travelers place Xi'an in the broader Chinese city-wide context of opportunistic theft rather than organised crime. For older travelers exploring Xi'an's old-city core, the standard defence applies: (1) crossbody zipped bag in front during Bell Tower / Drum Tower / City Wall walks; (2) phone in zipped inner pocket, never back pocket; (3) split valuables — carry only ¥200 and one card, passport and backup card in hotel safe; (4) bike rental on the City Wall is ¥45 for 100 minutes (published price) and includes a deposit — ensure deposit is returned in full on bike return. Xi'an's security is generally better than Beijing or Shanghai for pickpocket crime, but still maintain an alert posture.
scams.avoidance: Wear crossbody bag zipped in front during Bell Tower / Drum Tower / City Wall walks Never place phone in back pocket or outer backpack compartment Carry only ¥200 + one card; passport + backup in hotel safe Bike rental at City Wall is ¥45 for 100 min (published) — verify deposit returned in full If theft occurs, call 110 and 12315 (English-line consumer protection) within 24 hours
scams.location: Xi'an Bell Tower and Drum Tower squares, City Wall South Gate tourist crowd, Xi'an Ancient City Wall bike-rental area

scams.name: Jade 'Factory' Forced-Shopping Tour Stops
scams.description: Xi'an day-trip bus tours routinely include mandatory stops at 'government-certified jade factories' or 'traditional Chinese medicine museums' where tourists are held for 60–120 minutes of high-pressure sales. The guide's commission on purchases is 20–30%, so the 'free' tour's real revenue model depends on you buying. One traveler put it bluntly: 'Never buy anything that tour guides recommend, it's a pseudo-scam thing they have going with the shops where they get commission.' The jade sold is typically serpentine or dyed quartz sold as 'imperial jade' at 5–20x market prices. Community reports are blunt: 'We were promised a Chengdu tour in the itinerary, but ended up getting 4 scam spots in 2 days' — the model runs identically in Xi'an, Beijing, Chengdu, and other tourist cities. 2025 reports show the pattern continues unchanged. The 'government' certification is meaningless — the 'museum' is typically a private retail operation with government-issued business licenses (all businesses in China need one) that the guide presents as 'government-approved.' For older travelers, the only reliable defence is to BOOK TOURS WITH 'ZERO SHOPPING STOPS' IN WRITING before paying. Licensed small-group operators (Viator, GetYourGuide, Tiqets, and hotel-partnership Ctrip tours) offer this verification. Budget tours at ¥150–¥250 per person for a full-day Terracotta + surrounding sites trip ALWAYS include shopping stops — the economics don't work otherwise. Expect ¥300–¥500 per person for an honest full-day tour with no shopping. If you're already on a tour and it stops at a 'jade factory' or 'TCM clinic,' simply do not buy anything and wait 45–60 minutes for the bus to leave — the guide will be annoyed but has no legal power to compel purchases.
scams.avoidance: Book only tours with 'ZERO shopping stops' verified in writing before paying Use licensed operators: Viator, GetYourGuide, Tiqets, or hotel-partner Ctrip tours Expect ¥300–¥500 per person for honest full-day tours; anything lower includes shopping If already on a shopping-stop tour, simply don't buy — wait out the 45–60 min stop Report shopping-stop tours to 12315 (consumer protection English line) for documentation
scams.location: Along tour bus routes between Xi'an city centre and Terracotta Warriors / Huaqing Hot Spring, 'government jade museums' bundled with Terracotta day trips

scams.name: Tang Paradise / Huaqing Hot Spring 'Show' Ticket Scams
scams.description: Xi'an's tourism-geared evening shows — the Tang Dynasty Show at the Xi'an Hotel, the 'Song of Everlasting Sorrow' musical at Huaqing Palace, and the Tang Paradise evening water show — are popular with older travelers looking for a cultural evening. The scam variants: (1) hotel concierges push 'exclusive' show packages at ¥600–¥900 per person for shows that cost ¥298–¥498 direct; (2) street flyer touts outside the venues sell 'VIP' tickets that are actually standard seating at 1.5–2x face value; (3) 'Dinner + Show' bundles include a mediocre buffet at ¥400 that takes the total to ¥1,000+ per person when the show alone is ¥298. 2025 community guides confirm the official booking method also applies to evening shows: WeChat mini-programs for each venue are the legitimate channel. The Tang Dynasty Show (at the Xi'an Hotel) is the most-referenced for its packaging-vs-reality gap. A legitimate mid-tier ticket is ¥298 adult; 'VIP' is ¥398; dinner + show bundle is ¥598. Hotel concierge packages at ¥800–¥1,200 per person for the same experience are pure commission markups. Community reports reference the broader ecosystem of tourist-evening-entertainment overpricing common across Xi'an, Beijing, and Shanghai. For older travelers, the booking playbook: (1) book Tang Dynasty Show, Huaqing Palace evening show, or Tang Paradise water show directly via the official venue WeChat mini-program or Trip.com / Ctrip at published rates (¥298–¥498); (2) ignore hotel-concierge 'exclusive' packages above ¥600 per person; (3) for transportation, Metro Line 2 runs to Yanta area near Tang Paradise (¥5), and Huaqing Palace is reached via the Lintong tourist bus ¥8 + taxi ¥20; (4) verify 'dinner + show' components — a ¥300 buffet rarely delivers better than a ¥100 residential restaurant.
scams.avoidance: Book Tang Dynasty Show or Huaqing Palace show directly via venue WeChat mini-program or Trip.com Legitimate rates: ¥298 standard, ¥398 VIP, ¥598 dinner+show Ignore hotel-concierge packages over ¥600 per person — all are commission markups Metro Line 2 serves Tang Paradise area (¥5); Lintong tourist bus ¥8 + taxi ¥20 for Huaqing Palace For evening return, use DiDi (app-regulated) rather than venue taxi touts
scams.location: Tang Paradise (曲江大唐芙蓉园) evening water show area, Huaqing Palace hot spring evening shows, hotel-concierge Tang Dynasty Show packages

scams.name: Xi'an Tea Ceremony / Tea House Invitation
scams.description: The same Dong Bei criminal ring documented in Beijing and Shanghai tea-house scams extends to Xi'an's tourist core. The script is identical: attractive English-speaking Chinese women approach tourists at Bell Tower or Drum Tower asking to 'practice English' or 'take a photo together,' then invite the victim to a 'traditional Shaanxi tea ceremony' at a side-street venue. Bill: ¥2,000–¥5,000 per person for a 30-minute tea tasting. Community reports flag the Xi'an extension of the Beijing/Shanghai ring: 'You will also want to watch out for the tea house scam and possible variations on it (search the internet)' because it runs in every tier-1 Chinese tourist city. Community reports place the tea-house scam alongside the fake Terracotta Army and airport taxi scams as Xi'an's top three. The 2025 Xi'an pattern has some distinguishing features: the 'students' sometimes claim to be studying at Xi'an Jiaotong University or Shaanxi Normal University and offer to 'show you around the Muslim Quarter' as the opening move. The subsequent 'traditional tea house' invitation appears within 20 minutes. The venue is always on a quiet side street north or east of the Drum Tower area. The tea itself is real but overpriced 30–80x the residential rate. Community reports document the cross-Chinese-city consistency of the script. For older travelers visiting Xi'an, the rule is absolute: ANY stranger who approaches at Bell Tower, Drum Tower, Muslim Quarter, or Yongningmen (South Gate) with an invitation to 'tea,' 'Muslim Quarter tour,' 'traditional Shaanxi culture,' or 'cultural experience' is running this scam. Walk past with 'bu yao xie xie.' For genuine Xi'an tea culture, visit the Defuxiang tea market (south-west of Bell Tower) with posted prices, or a hotel-concierge-verified teahouse with English-language menus.
scams.avoidance: Walk past any stranger approaching at Bell Tower, Drum Tower, or Muslim Quarter entrance Never accept 'cultural experience' or 'tea ceremony' invitations from strangers For genuine Xi'an tea, visit Defuxiang tea market (posted prices) or hotel-verified venues Pay with credit card for chargeback leverage if trapped Call 12315 (English-line) and 110 (police) for both scam reports
scams.location: Bell Tower plaza, Drum Tower approach, Muslim Quarter entrance, around tourist-heavy Yong Ning Gate
